description: 💻 A fully functional local AWS cloud stack. Develop and test your cloud & Serverless apps offline

summary.one_liner: LocalStack is a cloud service emulator that runs AWS services locally in a single Docker container so you can develop and test AWS and serverless applications offline.
summary.what_it_does: Runs a local emulation of AWS services (such as Lambda, S3, DynamoDB, Kinesis, SQS, and SNS) inside one Docker container on a laptop or CI machine. The LocalStack CLI starts and manages that container from the command line. The README says Terraform and CDK configurations can be tested against it. A companion awslocal CLI is needed to interact with the local services. The Pro version adds more APIs and features, and a feature coverage page lists supported APIs. The README also points to user guides and docs. The README opens with a notice that this repository is archived and read-only, with development moved to a unified LocalStack image.
use_cases: test Terraform or CDK configurations without a real cloud account
run AWS integration tests in CI
learn AWS services on a laptop
how_to_run: Install Docker and make sure it is working.
brew install localstack/tap/localstack-cli  (macOS or Linux with Homebrew)
python3 -m pip install localstack  (PyPI route, run as a non-root user)
Alternatively, download the pre-built CLI binary from localstack/localstack-cli and extract it into a directory on your PATH.
localstack start -d  (starts the LocalStack Docker container)
Install the separate awslocal CLI to interact with the local services.
notable: Emulates many AWS services in a single container, so one local endpoint covers several services
Works with CDK and Terraform configurations for local testing
Installable via Homebrew, PyPI, or a standalone binary
Repository is archived; development has moved to the unified LocalStack image
caveats: This repository is archived and read-only; development has moved to the unified LocalStack image.
Must not be installed or run with sudo or as root.
Pro version provides additional APIs and features; the free Hobby plan is for non-commercial use.
keywords: test cloud apps without aws account
